name: Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon
description:
The Fincantieri Maritime Dual-Use Hackathon comes to San Francisco, October 16–18.

Following the first edition in Rome, which brought together 70+ participants, including Italian Navy engineers, and produced five working prototypes, the challenge now crosses the Atlantic to the Bay Area’s deep-tech ecosystem.

Over 48 hours, engineers, developers, founders, researchers and designers will form teams to build working solutions around real maritime and defense engineering challenges, with access to technical mentors, development hardware and potential opportunities to continue developing the strongest concepts beyond the event

Challenge Tracks

1. OT Cybersecurity & Blast Radius Analysis
2. Piping Layout Optimization
3. Software-Defined Vesse

Build with Real Hardware

Participants will have access to a selection of Qualcomm and Arduino technologies during the hackathon, including Snapdragon-powered laptops, edge AI and robotics development platforms, Arduino prototyping hardware and supporting developer tools.

These tools are intended for hands-on technical development. Participants with experience in areas such as software development, embedded systems, electronics, robotics, edge AI, computer vision or hardware prototyping will be best positioned to take full advantage of them.

Qualcomm and Arduino technologies will be introduced during the opening session so teams can quickly understand the available resources and integrate hardware, edge AI, computer vision, sensors or robotics into their prototypes.

Exact hardware configurations will be shared with participants ahead of the event

More Than a 48-Hour Hackathon

The goal is not only to build a prototype, but to identify ideas with the potential to continue developing after the event.

• Work on real Fincantieri challenges with potential relevance to future maritime and defense applications.
• Compete for a Qualcomm-powered laptop awarded to the winning team.
• Develop your concept beyond the hackathon: selected promising prototypes may have the opportunity to continue evolving.
• Access Fincantieri expertise: winning and particularly promising concepts may receive mentoring from Fincantieri’s network of experts to help further mature the solution and explore its potential application within Fincantieri.
• Connect with leading technical talent from industry, academia, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem

Partners & Ecosystem

[The hackathon is powered by Fincantieri](https://www.fincantieri.com/en), [Mind The Bridge](https://mindthebridge.com/)[and Silicon Mountain](https://www.linkedin.com/company/silicon-mtn/posts/?feedView=all).

Qualcomm is the main technology sponsor, supporting participants with hardware, development resources and technology expertise throughout the event.

Additional experts from Fincantieri, academia, industry, venture capital and the defense innovation ecosystem will support teams through mentoring and judgin

:
- • 48 hours of hands-on building and prototyping
• Real technical challenges provided by Fincantieri
• Access to Qualcomm and Arduino hardware and development resources
• Mentors and domain experts supporting teams throughout the event
• Collaboration with engineers, founders, and researchers
• A Qualcomm-powered laptop prize for the winning team
• Potential follow-on development opportunities for the most promising concepts

No maritime background is required. However, this is a hands-on technical hackathon, and participants should be ready to contribute directly through software development, AI/ML, embedded systems, cybersecurity, robotics, engineering, CAD/optimization, product design or prototyping.

Come with a team or find one at the event.

To help us maintain an accurate headcount, a $20 refundable deposit is required to reserve your spot. The deposit will be fully refunded when you attend the event.

Spots are limited — register early to secure your place.

name: ExecuTorch Hackathon
description:
NOTE: By registering for the Luma, you are submitting an application to participate. We will reach out on a rolling basis to let you know whether you've been accepted. There are a limited number of devices, we can support up to 200 participants.

This event is sponsored by Meta, Qualcomm, GitHub, Open Intelligence Foundation, and the PyTorch Foundation.

Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at [Founder’s Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026](https://opensourceaiweek.com/).

[Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm](https://www.qualcomm.com/developer), [Meta](https://www.meta.com/), [GitHub](https://github.com/), [the PyTorch Foundation](https://pytorch.org/foundation/), [and Open Intelligence Foundation](https://openintelligence.foundation/), this hands-on event will challenge teams [to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch](https://executorch.ai/)—an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.

Participants will work in teams of 3–5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.

Compute Track

Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.

Mobile + XR Track

Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.

IoT Track

Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino® VENTUNO™ Q boards, combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences. Choose from an assortment of modulinos and accessories to complete your project (available on a first come, first served basis).

To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3–5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.

Prizes

The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.

Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.

Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.

👉 Join here: https://discord.gg/A635v4hMSg

Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

About Open Intelligence Foundation

[The Open Intelligence Foundation](https://openintelligence.foundation/) is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in [open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week](https://opensourceaiweek.com/), a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.

About Founders, Inc.
[Founders, Inc.](https://f.inc/) backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

Snapdragon and Qualcomm branded products are products of Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. and/or its subsidiaries. Arduino and VENTUNO are trademarks or registered trademarks of Arduino S.r.l.

name: Bay Area AI+car hackathon
description:
Car AI Navigation Hackathon

Challenge: We have a mini city road with lanes, intersection and traffic signs. Your job is to use AI and a small autonomous car like the Donkeycar or equivalent (typically 1/16th scale or smaller RC car with a Raspberry Pi or equivalent and a camera controlling it) to navigate the "city", obeying signs and making it from one side to the other in the fastest time.

You must bring your own car, which should be ready to run, with compute and camera already onboard and working. The objective of the hackathon is to add AI "city" navigation to it.

You can use onboard AI, AI on your laptop via Wifi or AI in the cloud to help with the navigation. Think creatively about what kind of AI to use and what's the fastest way to do it!

This is not an event for spectators, nor will cars be provided to those who arrive without one. This is a hackathon, not a regular race. Come ready to hack!

name: Bitcoin India Tour- Goa Edition
description:
## Bitcoin India Tour – IIT Goa Edition

Bitcoin India Tour is a nationwide educational initiative bringing Bitcoin education to students across India. The tour explores the evolution of money, the problems with existing monetary systems, and the technology behind Bitcoin from first principles.

The IIT Goa Edition at the Indian Institute of Technology Goa brings an engaging learning experience for students interested in technology, computer science, economics, finance, and the future of money.

Starting with the fundamentals of money and moving into the technology behind Bitcoin, this session is designed to help students understand why Bitcoin was created, how it works, and what makes it different from traditional monetary systems

What You’ll Learn

• The evolution of money and how monetary systems have changed
• Inflation, purchasing power, and the importance of sound money
• Problems with the current monetary system
• What Bitcoin is and why it was created
• Bitcoin’s fixed supply and monetary properties
• How the Bitcoin network works
• Bitcoin mining, nodes, blocks, and network security
• Global Bitcoin adoption and real-world use cases
• Opportunities to learn, build, research, and contribute to the Bitcoin ecosyste

Who Should Attend?

name: Ethereum Classic Mumbai
description:
Ethereum and Ethereum Classic were once the same chain, until the DAO hard fork in 2016 sent them down separate paths. Ethereum later moved to Proof of Stake, while Classic stayed with Proof of Work. Ten years on, ETC enters its second decade, and every chain now faces new threats from quantum computers and AI.

We're a 15-minute walk from Ethereum Cypherpunk Congress #3 (https://congress.web3privacy.info/), and we invite you to this casual evening after it closes, the night before Devcon 8 opens, to pull up a chair and talk with Ethereum Classic developers and contributors.

Who It's For

Builders on any EVM chain, node runners and miners, Congress and Devcon people, and anyone curious about Ethereum Classic.

Let's Talk About

We think ETC, the EVM chain with the greatest hash rate, is going to make a comeback.

Quantum computers threaten the elliptic-curve signatures every chain uses today, but ETC's consensus rests on hash-based Proof of Work, which shouldn't need to be migrated. Mining a block takes real hardware and energy, and there are no validator keys to steal or forge. Wallets are a different story, and we still need to figure out post-quantum signatures for ETC accounts, looking to Ethereum's research on this for inspiration.

Coming straight from the Cypherpunk Congress, we also thought it would be interesting to talk about the cypherpunk ideas ETC was built on, like censorship resistance and protocol neutrality, and about EVM symbiosis, since ETC and Ethereum share the EVM and the same contracts, tools and builders can work on both.

We think ETC is an underdog with a bright future, carried through ten years by people who stayed for principles that never die

name: Can Regulated, Tokenized Assets Trade on Open Onchain Markets? Live Demo & Panel at Hong Kong Fintech Week
description:
Can Regulated, Tokenized Assets Trade on Open Onchain Markets? is a closed-door session co-hosted by OpenZeppelin and Ethereum Institutional during Hong Kong Fintech Week, limited to 30 senior participants from banks, market infrastructure, and regulated asset issuers.

Bringing regulated assets onto open onchain markets raises real questions for institutions, from who enforces eligibility rules to how investor data stays protected, and there are good reasons most activity still runs on permissioned platforms.

This session explores what is technically possible today and where the open questions remain. Through a live walkthrough of a tokenized money market fund trading on an open onchain market, we’ll look at how identity checks can run at every trade without personal data onchain, how a transfer agent can freeze an investor and have the market respect it on the next trade, and how a jurisdiction can be switched off while everyone else keeps trading.

A panel of industry experts then debates who should hold the keys when regulated assets meet open markets, and what it takes for institutions to go live. We close with a drinks reception.

Previous OpenZeppelin institutional events drew senior guests from firms including J.P. Morgan, Citi, UBS, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, BNY, Fidelity, Mastercard, Deloitte, and more

About Nara

Nara is a PayFi protocol offering a yield-bearing synthetic dollar backed by short-term financing against payment and receivables flows. Stablecoin payments are moving faster than the liquidity infrastructure around them. Stablecoins can settle near-instantly, but many payment companies still need to bridge delays between fiat collection, on/off-ramp conversion, local payout settlement, and stablecoin funding. That timing gap creates working-capital demand. Nara is the liquidity layer for the stablecoin economy because our goal is not simply to produce yield; our goal is to finance useful payment activity with transparent risk allocation.

About Hex Trust

Hex Trust is a fully-licensed and regulated financial institution for digital assets. It offers a full suite of Markets services, OTC trading, Custody, Staking and Investment Solutions to builders, investors, and service providers. Hex Trust have a global presence with offices in Singapore, Hong Kong, and Dubai.

The mission is to unlock ownership in decentralized markets, with a vision to secure the permissionless future.

About XDC Network

XDC Network is an enterprise-grade Layer 1 blockchain designed to support trade finance, payments, and the tokenization of real-world assets. Its EVM-compatible infrastructure provides fast settlement, low transaction costs, and energy-efficient performance, enabling institutions, businesses, and developers to build scalable blockchain solutions. Learn more at xinfin.org (https://xinfin.org).

We look forward to welcoming you for a morning of insightful discussions, meaningful connections and new opportunities at the intersection of Web3 and traditional finance.

description:
一、活動背景

Openvault 將於 2026 年 11 月 4 日 聯合 Techub News 在香港灣仔舉辦主題活動 「RWA 2.0：從資產上鏈到金融機會觸達」。

香港金融科技周 x StartmeupHK 是亞洲規模最大、影響力最廣的金融科技旗艦盛會。2026 年，兩大盛事進一步合流，以「Fintech Nexus：Bridging the World, Building the Future」為主題，圍繞 AI+、Finance+、Go Global 三大引擎展開，匯聚來自全球 120+ 經濟體的 45,000+ 行業領袖、1,000+ 演講嘉賓、800+ 贊助商／參展商／初創企業，以及 30+ 內地與國際貿易代表團。主論壇於 11 月 2–3 日在香港會議展覽中心舉行，隨後一週延伸至全港多個場地及粵港澳大灣區，舉辦數百場社區與周邊活動。

在金融科技週數百場周邊活動之中，「RWA 2.0」聚焦其中最接近落地的一段賽道：資產完成上鏈之後，金融機會如何真正觸達市場。

───────────────────────────

二、主題闡釋：為什麼是 RWA 2.0

過去兩年，RWA 完成了從概念驗證到批量發行的第一步。政府數字債券、代幣化基金、私募信貸等項目相繼落地，香港的監管框架與沙盒機制亦逐步成型。

資產上鏈解決的是「發行」問題。​ 債券、基金、私募信貸、商業地產等傳統資產透過代幣化進入鏈上世界，獲得了可分割、可編程、可跨境流轉的新形態。

但發行不等於流動性，上鏈不等於被配置。​ 分銷渠道能否打通持牌體系？專業投資者如何在合規框架下完成認購與轉讓？二級市場的深度從何而來？這些「最後一公里」的問題，決定 RWA 是停留在技術敘事，還是成為真實的資產類別。

這正是 RWA 2.0 的命題：從「能發行」走向「有人買」。​ 活動將匯聚資產發行方、資產管理機構、持牌交易平台與合規專業人士，圍繞分銷機制、流動性建設與投資者觸達路徑，分享一線實踐與監管觀察。

name: London Workshop: Vaults in Practice – How Financial Institutions Capture Onchain Yield
description:
This workshop provides a structured, case-study-driven deep dive into onchain vaults as the key primitive of DeFi and tokenized capital markets, led by Steakhouse Financial.

Starting from familiar concepts such as funds and ETFs, the session explains how vaults represent the next step in the evolution of asset management — combining programmable execution, non-custodial design, and real-time risk management. Participants will gain a practical understanding of how vaults work, how they differ from traditional investment vehicles, and why they are increasingly adopted by institutions.

The discussion then moves from fundamentals into live production environments, examining how vaults are deployed, operated, and integrated today. This includes institutional use cases such as platform integrations, as well as operational and compliance considerations when running vault strategies in regulated contexts.

From there, the workshop explores where vault management is expanding next, using concrete production case studies curated and operated by Steakhouse Financial:

• RWA as collateral (Fasanara mF-ONE)
• Fixed-term lending and yield structuring via Pendle
• Leveraged vault strategies (Steakhouse High Yield Turbo)

By the end of the session, attendees will have a clear, example-driven understanding of how vaults are used in practice today, and how the frontier of vault management is shaping the next generation of institutional onchain products.

About Steakhouse Financial
Steakhouse Financial is the leading curator on DeFi Money Markets (Morpho, Kamino), building earn products for the future of the stablecoin economy. Steakhouse Financial operates at the intersection of real world assets, protocol design, and data-driven DeFi portfolio management. They aspire to empower the world with institutional-grade DeFi tools to raise, manage and distribute the capital they need to make a difference.

For questions, please contact: mail@blockstories.io

## bitcoin++'s Insider Edition 「bitcoin++'s Insider Edition」は、ビットコインの技術カンファレンス「bitcoin++」が発信するWebマガジンです。世界各地でビットコインをつくる開発者・技術者たちの仕事にスポットを当て、bitcoin++のコミュニティ内外で起きていることを伝えています。 今回のミートアップは、そのInsider Editionの名を冠して東京で開催します。 bitcoin++'s Insider Edition is the web magazine of bitcoin++, the technical Bitcoin conference series. It showcases the work of Bitcoin builders and tech talent around the world, with stories from across the bitcoin++ community and beyond. This Tokyo meetup is held under the Insider Edition name. Web: insider.btcpp.dev (https://insider.btcpp.dev/) X: @btcinsider__ (https://x.com/btcinsider__) English below↓ ## ビットコインビルダーと過ごす、東京の夜 Arkプロトコルの実装「Bark」を開発する Second の Matthew Vuk さんたちの来日に合わせ、日本のビットコイン開発者 Joe Miyamoto さんをお迎えして、Tokyo Bitcoin Base（TBB）で開催します。 【イベント概要】 日時：2026年11月11日（水）19:00〜21:30（予定） 会場：Tokyo Bitcoin Base 参加費：無料 言語：英語 ゲスト：Matthew Vuk（Second）、Joe Miyamoto ほか こんな方におすすめ • ビットコインの開発やプロトコルに関わっている、または興味がある方 • ビットコインのスケーリング技術について、つくっている本人から話を聞きたい方 • 海外のビットコイン開発者と交流したい方 【タイムテーブル】 詳細は後日お知らせします。 ※プログラムや内容は予告なく変更になる場合があります。 【ゲストについて】 Matthew Vuk（Second／Researcher） Arkプロトコルの実装「Bark」を開発するSecondのリサーチャーです。カナダのウィルフリッド・ローリエ大学でビットコインクラブを立ち上げ、大学生向けのビットコイン開発者教育にも取り組んできました。bitcoin++などの技術カンファレンスにも登壇しています。2026年には、アフリカのモバイルマネーをArkで決済する取り組みにも関わっています。 Joe Miyamoto（ビットコイン開発者） バイオインフォマティクスの研究者からビットコイン開発者に転身し、国内外の暗号資産取引所で開発に携わってきました。.NETでライトニングネットワークを扱うライブラリ「DotNetLightning」や、ライトニングのLoop機能を汎用化した「NLoop」の開発者です。Bitcoin Tokyo 2024では技術ワークショップを担当し、パネルのモデレーターも務めました。 Andrei（ビットコイン開発者） ## A Tokyo Evening with Bitcoin Builders Matthew Vuk of Second, the team building Bark (an implementation of the Ark protocol), and other builders are coming to Tokyo. To mark the occasion, Tokyo Bitcoin Base (TBB) is hosting this event with them and Japanese Bitcoin developer Joe Miyamoto. 【Event Overview】 Date & Time: Wednesday, November 11, 2026,
- 19:00–21:30 (tentative) Venue: Tokyo Bitcoin Base Admission: Free Language: English Guests: Matthew Vuk (Second), Joe Miyamoto, and more Recommended For • Anyone working on or interested in Bitcoin development and protocols • Anyone who wants to hear about Bitcoin scaling from the people building it • Anyone who wants to connect with Bitcoin developers from abroad 【Schedule】 Details will be announced soon. ※ Event details are subject to change without prior notice. 【About the Guests】 Matthew Vuk (Researcher, Second) Matthew is a researcher at Second, the team behind Bark, an implementation of the Ark protocol. He founded the Bitcoin club at Wilfrid Laurier University in Canada and has worked on onboarding university students into Bitcoin development. He speaks at technical conferences such as bitcoin++, and in 2026 helped bring Ark-based settlement to mobile-money systems in Africa. Joe Miyamoto (Bitcoin Developer) Joe moved from bioinformatics research into Bitcoin development, and has worked as a developer at both domestic and international cryptocurrency exchanges. He is the creator of DotNetLightning, a library for working with the Lightning Network on .NET, and NLoop, a generic implementation of Lightning Loop. At Bitcoin Tokyo 2024 he ran a technical workshop and moderated panel sessions. Andrei (Bitcoin Developer)

name: The Fireblocks Roundtable: Moving Money Across Africa
description: Fireblocks and Linum Labs are bringing together a select group of the Fireblocks community for an afternoon of focused conversation at The Vineyard, at the foot of Table Mountain, followed by drinks and bites. Moving money across Africa is still slow, expensive and fragmented. FX friction, multi-day settlement and layered intermediary fees hold back trade, remittances and treasury operations across the continent. This roundtable is a private forum for our key partners and customers to ask whether stablecoins and digital assets can fix it, and what it would take to make that work in practice. What we’ll explore • The real cost of cross-border payments and FX across African corridors • Where stablecoins and digital assets are already improving speed and settlement • Regulatory, liquidity and on/off-ramp realities • What institutions need to move from pilots to production The format • 4:00 PM: Presentation • Afterwards: Drinks and bites, to continue the conversation

description:
## Whitepaper Reading Club × Open Note Labs November Edition: Uniswap v4 Hooks For November's edition of Whitepaper Reading Club, we're partnering with Open Note Labs (https://on-labs.org/)to dive into Uniswap v4 Hooks and the expanding design space they enable. Uniswap v4 introduces hooks: customizable smart contracts that execute at specific points in a liquidity pool's lifecycle. By allowing developers to extend pool behavior without modifying the underlying protocol, hooks open up new possibilities for automated market makers, liquidity management, and onchain financial applications. We'll explore the architecture behind Uniswap v4, how hooks work, and what this new levels can be unlocked for the future of programmable finance. Discussion topics include: • Hooks and the Uniswap v4 architecture • Dynamic fees, custom accounting, and liquidity management • New mechanisms for market making and onchain trading • Emerging applications and design possibilities enabled by hooks Reading: Uniswap v4 Core Whitepaper (https://app.uniswap.org/whitepaper-v4.pdf

Moderator: Ryan Hall Ryan has been at Chainlink working on their smart contract since 2018. He then lea smart contract development at Lagrange and now at Polymarket. He's one of the best engineers that I know and knows Solidity like the back of his hand :

About Whitepaper Reading Club We are a community of founders, researchers, and builders across Singapore, Malaysia, San Francisco, Bangkok, New York, Lagos, Taipei, and Hong Kong. We meet in person every month to read, discuss, and pressure-test the latest blockchain papers, protocols, and technical ideas. name: Bitcoin on Sui: Getting Started with Hashi
description: Bitcoin is the largest pool of idle capital in crypto, and most of it never moves, because using it anywhere else has meant handing it to a custodian or a wrapped-token bridge. Hashi is Sui's answer. Your BTC stays on Bitcoin, held at an address controlled jointly by Hashi's validator committee, which signs with threshold MPC, and an independent guardian layer. Against it, hBTC is minted on Sui and works across Sui apps. Burn the hBTC and the BTC is released back on Bitcoin. Hashi is now live on Sui mainnet in a phased rollout, partners first, backed by more than $500 million in commitments from over 20 partners including Anchorage Digital. In early November about 9.6 hBTC had been minted onchain, and you can watch that number grow. This session explains how Hashi works under the hood and gets you building with it. We read the live mainnet deployment directly: the Hashi object, the deposit and withdrawal queues, the committee and the hBTC supply. Then we use the Hashi TypeScript SDK on testnet with Bitcoin signet to run the full user journey: generate a personal Bitcoin deposit address for a Sui account, send signet BTC to it, follow the deposit through committee approval until hBTC is minted, and request a withdrawal back to Bitcoin. You build hBTC Desk, a small app that runs the testnet round trip and shows the live mainnet numbers beside it. What You'll Learn - How Hashi keeps BTC on Bitcoin: per-account deposit addresses, joint control by the validator committee and the guardian layer, threshold MPC signing, and how hBTC is minted and burned - What is live today: reading the mainnet package, the deposit and withdrawal queues and the hBTC supply with GraphQL, and what a phased rollout means for builders - The SDK: @mysten/hashi, generating a deposit address, submitting a deposit, tracking its status, and requesting or cancelling a withdrawal - Building on hBTC: using it like any other Sui coin in your own Move code and programmable transactions, with 8 decimals and integer base units from end to end - Honest limits: the SDK is pre-1.0 and not yet wired to mainnet, deposits wait for Bitcoin confirmations and a time delay, and how to show pending states so nobody pays twice - How to ship hBTC Desk: deposit signet BTC, watch hBTC arrive on Sui testnet, withdraw back to a Bitcoin address, and compare it with the live mainnet numbers Who Should Attend - DeFi builders who want Bitcoin as collateral in lending, trading or vaults - Wallet and payments teams that want to hold and move BTC inside Sui apps - Developers who joined the bridging and CCTP sessions and want the Bitcoin side of the story - Bitcoin holders curious how BTC can be used on another chain without giving up custody to a single company What to Bring - Laptop with Node.js 22+ and pnpm, and the latest @mysten/sui and @mysten/hashi - A Sui testnet wallet - A Bitcoin wallet that supports signet, such as Sparrow. We share a signet faucet in class - Basic TypeScript. No Bitcoin scripting required Join us at SuiHub to learn, build, and connect with fellow developers pushing the boundaries of the Sui ecosystem.

name: Race Against the Machine: AI, Quantum and the Future of Bitcoin
description:
## Intro

Almost everything we trust online, from banking and web traffic to messaging and digital identity, rests on public-key cryptography. Two threats are now calling that very foundation into question. Quantum computers could break today's signatures and key exchange, with the hardware required shrinking steadily. AI could reach the same result with breakthroughs in mathematics, and it is already helping quantum attacks along by optimizing the circuits behind them. 

The synergy between them is unmistakable, and even the post-quantum schemes meant to replace today's cryptography may not be safe either. With finance and the internet facing a long, fragmented migration, the stakes are highest where cryptography protects value directly. Cryptocurrencies add their own exposure: public keys sit on a public ledger, assets are bearer instruments, and theft is irreversible. Given Bitcoin's history, the challenge is particularly acute: every serious option (do nothing, freeze, force a deadline) violates a principle the Bitcoin community cares about, and the work must start before the threat is visible.

Join us at this interdisciplinary event where AI, quantum and Bitcoin experts come together in a novel panel to discuss the technical foundations of this challenge and its potential solutions

With a PhD from Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and a background developing AI products, Wadim now works at Bundesdruckerei focusing on applied cybersecurity in the era of Quantum and AI. His focus goes beyond hardware. AI-driven discoveries and algorithmic improvements can reduce the resources needed to challenge today’s cryptography. Understanding these shifts is essential to assessing quantum threats and making informed security decisions.

name: Whitepaper Reading [SF] - Defi Topics: No Place to Hide & Active Liquidity On Chain
description: Discussion Topics As more trading moves through private RPCs and protected submission channels, the question is how much safety those protections actually buy. No Place to Hide examines three years of activity across six chains and finds sandwich attacks against supposedly protected transactions on four of them. The exposure comes from order-flow auctions, validators, applications, reorgs, and even an RPC bug. We’ll ask what “protected” should mean when keeping a trade out of the public mempool still leaves multiple ways for attackers to see it coming, and whether protection can hold without securing the full path from wallet to execution. We’ll also cover Active Liquidity On Chain, a study of proprietary AMMs across Solana, Base, and Monad. These venues let a single operator supply inventory and update prices without waiting for a trade, helping them avoid the stale quotes that arbitrageurs exploit in passive AMMs. The paper finds better prices for flow used as a proxy for retail trading, alongside pricing that varies by counterparty and evidence of quotes that worsen at execution. The core discussion is whether tighter spreads justify opaque pricing rules, and how aggregators should route trades when the price they see may differ from the price users receive. Reading Overview • No Place to Hide: Where private transaction protections fail, and what it takes to secure the full path from wallet to execution. • Active Liquidity On Chain: How proprietary AMMs improve pricing, and the trade-offs around transparency, routing, and execution quality. Full Documents • No Place to Hide (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.28115) • Active Liquidity On Chain (https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.38056) Format • 10 minutes of silent reading to start. • Discussion first, with no panels. • Bring questions—technical depth is welcomed. • Short notes and key takeaways shared after the session. About Whitepaper Reading Club Whitepaper Reading Club is a community of 800 builders, founders, and researchers across Singapore, Malaysia, San Francisco, Lagos, Bangkok, and New York. The community meets in person every month to discuss the latest blockchain projects. The club creates detailed, easy-to-understand summaries for each paper and has held more than 70 sessions since June 2023, covering topics from Account Abstraction, Parallel Chains, and EIPs to the Bitcoin ecosystem and AI × crypto. It is ecosystem-agnostic and not for profit, with a strong focus on projects with technical, product, or social innovations. Dimes, our community partner, connects builders with the people, resources, and support to turn ideas into reality. Our host venue, localhost, is Dimes’ co-working and event space in downtown San Francisco, created for builders to meet, share ideas, and connect. We’re excited to host this event with Whitepaper Reading Club. #Crypto

description:
SuperPioneros · Encuentro #139

📅 Lunes 16 de noviembre · 17:30h
📍 Madrid Innovation Lab · Madrid

Durante años hemos hablado de las posibilidades de Blockchain. Pero ahora que empresas, instituciones y desarrolladores empiezan a construir soluciones reales, surge una nueva pregunta:

👉 ¿Qué aporta realmente una Blockchain regulada frente a otras infraestructuras?

El próximo 16 de noviembre celebramos nuestro Encuentro #139 de SuperPioneros, donde reuniremos a empresas, instituciones, emprendedores y builders para debatir sobre el papel de las nuevas infraestructuras Blockchain L1 reguladas y las oportunidades que abren para el ecosistema.

Y lo haremos junto a ISBE, la iniciativa de Alastria para impulsar una infraestructura Blockchain pública permisionada, diseñada para facilitar el desarrollo de casos de uso empresariales

🎙️ LOS PROTAGONISTAS

Contaremos con:

👉 Miguel Calero, Director Ejecutivo de ISBE, quien compartirá la visión del proyecto, su evolución y las oportunidades que ofrece a empresas y desarrolladores.

Próximamente anunciaremos nuevos invitados y empresas con casos de uso reales

🔥 ¿DE QUÉ HABLAREMOS?

Queremos abrir una conversación que vaya más allá de la tecnología.

⚡ Blockchain regulada vs. otras infraestructuras. ¿Qué ventajas ofrece realmente y cuándo tiene sentido utilizarla?

🏦 Empresas e instituciones. ¿Qué necesitan para adoptar Blockchain con confianza y seguridad jurídica?

🪙 Tokenización y nuevos modelos de negocio. ¿Qué oportunidades aparecen para sectores como finanzas, inmobiliario, energía o industria?

🚀 Casos de uso reales. ¿Qué están construyendo las empresas y qué barreras encuentran para llevar sus proyectos a producción?

🤝 Talento y oportunidades. ¿Cómo conectar a las empresas que necesitan soluciones con los builders capaces de desarrollarlas?

No queremos únicamente escuchar presentaciones.

Queremos generar debate, compartir experiencias y descubrir qué podemos construir juntos

Con Bit2Me como desafío número 1 de SuperPioneros, seguimos impulsando una Comunidad de más de 80.000 innovadores que conecta talento, empresas, instituciones e inversores alrededor de la IA, Blockchain, Web3 y las tecnologías emergentes.

Porque el futuro de Blockchain no dependerá únicamente de la tecnología.

Dependerá de los problemas que seamos capaces de resolver con ella.

name: SC Ventures Lab Crawl Panel 4: Policy Rewiring: When AI Moves Money
description:
About Event AI agents are no longer just recommending payments. With stablecoins and programmable rails, they can initiate and settle them too. That raises questions existing rules weren’t written for. What should an agent be allowed to do on its own, when does a human need to approve, and who is accountable when something goes wrong? This session brings together banking, blockchain and regulatory perspectives to look at the permissions, oversight and safeguards needed before agents can be trusted to move real value. On th

:
- • From recommend to execute: what changes when an AI agent can actually move money • Delegated authority: spending limits, approved counterparties and the thresholds that should trigger human approval • Know your agent: how agents are identified, authenticated and tied back to the person or business they act for • When things go wrong: liability for errors, fraud or a compromised agent, and what happens when a stablecoin transaction can’t be reversed • Compliance by design: building sanctions screening, AML checks and audit trails into the transaction itself • Are current rules fit for purpose, or does agentic finance need a new rulebook? Part 1: The Global Tokenisation Landscape Title: From Pilot to Production: Markets, Infrastructure and Regulation in 2026 and beyond Tokenisation is moving from pilot projects into regulated commercial activity across several jurisdictions, marking an important inflection point for digital assets in 2026. With Singapore and Hong Kong serving as key financial and family office hubs in Asia, developments in tokenised real-world assets, stablecoins and financial market infrastructure are creating new opportunities and considerations for financial institutions, private bankers, family offices and investors. RHTLaw Asia invites you to join our industry and legal experts as we examine the global tokenisation landscape, focusing on the transition from experimentation to commercial implementation, and the regulatory, market and legal developments shaping its future

Key Discussion Topics 1. Global Policy Developments: The Industry View An examination of regulatory and policy developments across the United States, Singapore, Hong Kong and the UAE, including stablecoin legislation, tokenised securities and the growing need for cross-border regulatory recognition and interoperable standards. 2. Market and Infrastructure Reality Check A closer look at the rise of tokenised securities and institutional products, including tokenised investment funds and private credit. The discussion will examine infrastructure choices, public versus permissioned blockchains, settlement systems, interoperability risks and the liquidity challenges facing tokenised private assets. 3. Legal Implications for Investors Tokenisation does not change the underlying legal character of an asset. We will examine the distinction between tokens representing direct ownership rights and synthetic exposure, together with the legal considerations and potential risks for issuers and investors. 4. Panel Discussion and Q&A An interactive discussion bringing together industry and legal perspectives on the opportunities and challenges of tokenisation, and what these developments mean for the future of digital assets in Asia

Coming Up: Part 2 – Tokenised Assets: The Investor's Playbook From Insight to Action: Access, Ownership, Risk and Legacy 3 December 2026 | 3:00 pm – 5:00 pm Building on the global developments covered in Part 1, the second session will focus on how private investors and family offices can participate in tokenised assets, including product structures, custody arrangements, investor protection, legal ownership, tax considerations and succession planning. From understanding what's changing to exploring what to do about it. We look forward to welcoming you.

description: English follows Japanese 「あたらしい経済」と「KudasaiJP」が共同運営する企業向けWeb3コミュニティ「Web3 Business Hub（WBH）」では、Web3ビジネスの発展に参考となるセミナーを毎月開催しています。 11月のテーマは「Hyperliquidとオンチェーンファイナンスの歴史」です。 ブロックチェーンを活用した金融サービスは、BitcoinやEthereumの登場を経て、DEX、レンディング、ステーブルコイン、デリバティブなど、さまざまな領域へと発展してきました。特に2020年のDeFi Summer以降、スマートコントラクトによる金融機能の実装が急速に進み、従来の金融機関や中央集権的な取引所を介さない、新しい金融市場の可能性が示されてきました。 その進化を象徴するプロジェクトの一つが、オンチェーンのデリバティブ取引を中心に成長してきた Hyperliquid です。独自のLayer 1ブロックチェーン上で、高速な取引処理とオンチェーンのオーダーブックを実現し、従来の中央集権型取引所（CEX）に近い取引体験を提供することで、分散型金融の新たな可能性を切り拓いています。さらに、HyperEVMによるアプリケーションの拡張など、単なる取引プラットフォームを超えた金融エコシステムへの発展も注目されています。 一方で、オンチェーン金融の発展には、流動性の確保、価格形成、セキュリティ、分散性、ガバナンス、規制対応など、さまざまな課題も存在します。DeFiはこれまでの歴史の中で何を実現し、何を課題として残してきたのでしょうか。そしてHyperliquidのような新しいプラットフォームは、従来の金融市場や暗号資産取引所のあり方をどこまで変えるのでしょうか。 今回のWeb3 Business Hubでは、DeFiの誕生からDeFi Summer、DEXやオンチェーンデリバティブの進化、そしてHyperliquidの成長に至るまで、オンチェーン金融の歴史を振り返ります。あわせて、Hyperliquidの仕組みや成長の背景、既存の金融サービスとの違い、今後の事業機会と課題についても整理します。 金融サービスは、どこまでオンチェーンで実現できるのか。 Hyperliquidを通じて、オンチェーン金融の現在地と、金融機関・Web3事業者・一般企業にとっての新たな可能性を、ゲストの藤田氏と参加者の皆さまと一緒に考えます。 藤田拓也氏プロフィール Hyperliquid Japan 技術渉外 / SubEtha Founder 筑波大学社会工学類卒。HashHubでブロックチェーンエンジニアとして経験を積み、MycelやHiveFiなどのWeb3プロジェクトに参画。クロスチェーン、DeFi、AI×ブロックチェーン領域の開発に携わり、ETHGlobal、HackAtom、Colosseumなどのハッカソンで受賞。Cosmos JapanのAdminとしてコミュニティ運営に携わり、現在はHyperliquid JapanのAdmin・技術渉外として活動。自ら立ち上げたAIエージェント向けプライバシー決済プロトコル「SubEtha」では、代表としてプロダクト開発を進めている。 セミナー概要 Hyperliquidとオンチェーンファイナンスの歴史 日時：2026年11月18日（水）19:00 開場／19:30 開始（20:30〜ネットワーキング、21:30 イベント終了予定） 会場：幻冬舎3号館 3F Hub（WBH）」について​「あたらしい経済」と「KudasaiJP」が共同運営する、企業向けWeb3コミュニティです。現在以下の会員限定コンテンツを企業様にご提供しております。ぜひご参加ください。 [実施内容] ・イベント開催（毎月1回以上/リアル or オンライン） ・ネットワーキングイベント開催（四半期毎/リアル） ・スポットコンサルティング機会の提供（毎月/指定日に参加いただける方） https://www.neweconomy.jp/features/wbh ---- The “Web3 Business Hub (WBH)”, a corporate-focused Web3 community jointly operated by Atarashii Keizai and KudasaiJP, hosts monthly seminars designed to provide practical insights for advancing Web3 business initiatives. The theme for October is “Hyperliquid and the History of Onchain Finance” Blockchain-based financial services have evolved significantly since the emergence of Bitcoin and Ethereum, expanding into various areas such as decentralized exchanges (DEXs), lending, stablecoins, and derivatives. In particular, since DeFi Summer in 2020, the rapid development of smart contract-based financial applications has demonstrated the potential for new financial markets that operate without relying on traditional financial intermediaries or centralized exchanges. One of the projects representing this evolution is Hyperliquid, which has gained significant attention through its focus on on-chain derivatives trading. Built on its own Layer 1 blockchain, Hyperliquid combines high-speed transaction processing with an on-chain order book, offering a trading experience comparable to that of centralized exchanges (CEXs) while exploring new possibilities for decentralized finance. With the expansion of its ecosystem through HyperEVM, Hyperliquid is also evolving beyond a trading platform into a broader on-chain financial ecosystem. At the same time, the development of on-chain finance continues to face challenges, including liquidity, price discovery, security, decentralization, governance, and regulatory compliance. What has DeFi achieved throughout its history, and what challenges remain unresolved? To what extent can emerging platforms such as Hyperliquid transform traditional financial markets and the role of cryptocurrency exchanges? For this edition of Web3 Business Hub, we will explore the history of on-chain finance, from the early days of DeFi and DeFi Summer to the evolution of DEXs and on-chain derivatives, culminating in the rise of Hyperliquid. We will also examine Hyperliquid's architecture, the factors behind its growth, how it differs from traditional financial services, and the opportunities and challenges that lie ahead. How much of the financial system can ultimately move on-chain? Through the lens of Hyperliquid, we will explore the current state and future potential of on-chain finance, as well as the new opportunities it may create for financial institutions, Web3 businesses, and enterprises. name: REWIRED: A Forum on Stablecoins and Agentic Payments
description:
19 November 2026 ·
- 12:30–17:00 SGT · Lunch provided · Approval within 24 hours Feeling lucky? Several Fitbit Air trackers are up for grabs, plus the new Fitbit Edge, launched just weeks ago. Intro This year's Singapore FinTech Festival looks at the forces rewiring global finance. Payments is where that rewiring is most visible: AI agents are starting to spend real money, more of it settles in stablecoins, and the rails are arriving faster than the controls. REWIRED brings together the people building and running payments to work out what comes next: • Who authorises an agent to pay? • What stops the payment when the agent is compromised? • Where does the margin sit when software pays software? Speakers Featuring speakers from AWS, Visa, Mastercard, BVNK, BlockSec, FXC Intelligence, Sunrate and Cobo You make the calls • Run the incident. MAS's SAFR framework proposes that no agent action executes until it has been declared, authorised and assessed. Test that idea on a live case: an agent with payment authority has been manipulated and transfers are queued. Vote on what stops the money, then put the panel on the spot. • Pick the rails. Card networks are piloting agent checkout across APAC, and Visa already settles in stablecoins at a US$7 billion annualised run rate. Cards, stablecoins or both: argue who owns checkout when the buyer is software. • Settle the bank question. Everyone agrees you need a bank to cash out. Beyond that, decide whether banks still own anything when agents pay: programmable money, accountability for the agent, or 24/7 settlement. Ask in English or Chinese on Slido at any time. Who should attend Anyone building, running or investing in payments, stablecoins or AI-driven commerce. Agenda (SGT)

name: Quantum Security for Digital Assets
description:
As quantum computing accelerates toward cryptographically relevant milestones, the digital asset ecosystem faces an architectural reckoning. Public blockchains like Ethereum are charting multi-year post-quantum cryptography (PQC) roadmaps and custody providers are testing PQC in practice, but protecting distributed ledgers, critical infrastructure and cross-border digital economies requires coordinated action across industry, regulators and government agencies. This afternoon brings them into one room. We open with Project Eagle, a live PQC pilot co-led by Safeheron and the Responsible Fintech Institute, in which banks and regulators across multiple jurisdictions test quantum-resistant multi-party computation (MPC) signing on a public testnet. A panel of leaders from law, law enforcement technology, smart-city jurisdictions and quantum security then examines signature scheme migration, systemic risks to custody and key management, and the public-private standards needed before Q-Day. We close with Ethereum's post-quantum roadmap and what it means for institutions, followed by networking. EVENT AGENDA

name: Designing Trust in the Digital Economy
description:
## Introduction As AI reshapes how we build, create, and transact, trust has become the currency that matters most. Join us for an event on using AI to build trust across the new money era, content, and AI itself with keynotes, a hands-on AI skills challenge, and networking to wrap up the evenin

:
- Keynote talks from industry voices Live Q&A with speakers Community networkin

Speakers Peter Zheng is Head of Design at OKX, where his team designs the products more than 120 million customers use to trade, pay and save. Over 20 years, his career has taken him from East to West, through agencies including W+K, TBWA\Media Arts Lab and Ogilvy, and in-house at Google, Samsung and Meta. Working across cultures has taught him that good ideas start with listening. As AI changes how products get made, he is helping his team move from designing screens to designing systems, with people at the center. Topic Intro: More of our financial lives now happen on a phone, at any hour, and soon with AI doing some of the work for us. None of that matters if people don’t feel safe enough to use it. Crypto gave us new ways to prove things. Anyone can check a transaction on a blockchain, and exchanges publish reports showing they hold customers’ funds. Yet people still hesitate before they hit “confirm.” Proof and protection are different things, and design has to close the distance between them. In this session, Peter shares how OKX designs for trust, from showing people how they’re protected to helping them understand what they’re agreeing to before it's final. He’ll also look at what changes when we start handing some of those decisions to an AI agent. Pearly Tan is Content Systems Director at OKX, where she is leading the shift from content design as a service to content as a scalable system for global digital products. She previously led Global Content Design at OKX and led the build of award-winning experiences across Meta Reality Labs, TikTok Shop and Bank of Singapore. Topic intro: As digital products expand, users face more opportunities, choices and information. They also face more uncertainty, emotion and risk. Trust must be built throughout the experience, especially when people are deciding whether to explore, act, or ask for help. Doing this at scale requires a shift from relying on specialists for every decision to building systems that make trustworthy choices easier across the organisation. This session explores how content systems can: • Give users the information they need, when they need it • Build trust with transparency that is relevant and proportionate • Direct expertise to moments where uncertainty carries real consequences • Help every team make sound, responsible decisions at scale Pearly will discuss OKX’s content transformation and how AI-enabled systems can help more people become responsible trust builders. Ben Bowes is the Director of Product Design at Open Government Products (OGP), where he helps teams make government products effective, enjoyable and worthy of people’s trust. He thinks public service is where the best designers belong, making everyday life better for the people around them. As AI reshapes how we build and create, Ben believes people must remain at the heart of what we design and why. Topic intro: When AI can make almost anything look and sound convincing, how do we know what’s real and who to trust? From everyday encounters to government services, design shapes how trust is built, tested and sometimes exploited. With so much uncertainty, how can public institutions earn our trust? Maybe a little doubt is part of what makes trust possible

Who should attend • Designers who are curious about how AI is reshaping trust in technolog

name: Finding Satoshi: filmvertoning & borrel
description:
Wie is Satoshi Nakamoto? Het is een van de grootste onopgeloste raadsels van onze tijd, en op zaterdag 21 november duiken we er samen in. De Dutch Bitcoin Embassy nodigt je uit voor een besloten vertoning van Finding Satoshi in Flora Filmtheater in Den Haag, met popcorn bij de film en een borrel na afloop

Over de film Finding Satoshi (2026) volgt onderzoeksjournalist William D. Cohan en privédetective Tyler Maroney tijdens een forensisch onderzoek van vier jaar naar de herkomst van Bitcoin. Onderweg spreken ze mensen uit het hart van de sector, onder wie Michael Saylor en Joseph Lubin. De film gaat net zo goed over de ideeën achter Bitcoin als over de vraag wie het heeft bedacht. Regie: Matthew Miele en Tucker Tooley · 101 minuten · Engels gesproke

Wat is inbegrepen Toegang tot de besloten vertoning in de filmzaal van Flora Popcorn bij de film Borrel na afloop met twee drankjes Een middag met Bitcoiners, ondernemers en nieuwsgierigen Popcorn en drankjes worden je aangeboden door onze sponsor Blockrise

Programma 13.30 uur: inloop 14.00 uur: welkom en start film Rond 15.45 uur: einde film Aansluitend: borrel bij Flora, tot ongeveer 17.30 uu

Voor wie Voor iedereen: of je al jaren in Bitcoin zit, net begint of gewoon nieuwsgierig bent. Na de aftiteling praten we verder tijdens de borrel. Neem gerust iemand mee

Praktisch Flora Filmtheater, De Constant Rebecquestraat 55, Den Haag (Regentessekwartier). Openbaar vervoer: RandstadRail 3 en tram 11 op vijf minuten lopen, RandstadRail 4 op tien minuten. Parkeren kan in de wijk en je fiets zet je voor de deur. De film start stipt om 14.00 uur, dus kom op tijd

Tickets Early Bird €35 · Regulier €42 Inclusief film, popcorn en twee drankjes. De zaal telt 50 stoelen, dus wees er op tijd bij

Over de Dutch Bitcoin Embassy De Dutch Bitcoin Embassy brengt ondernemers, bouwers en nieuwsgierigen rond Bitcoin samen in Den Haag. Na de uitverkochte vertoning van DirtyCoin in 2025 is dit onze tweede filmmiddag. We kijken ernaar uit je (weer) te zien. Vragen? Mail info@dutchbitcoinembassy.co

name: Trust Infrastructure for the Tokenization Era : Travel Rule and AML
description: As digital assets transition from pilot experiments (STOs and RWAs) into institutional finance, KYC and AML compliance are no longer merely back-office burdens—they are the core trust infrastructure and prerequisites for new business. Ahead of South Korea’s full implementation of the Travel Rule (effective February 2027)—which lowers exemption thresholds and tightens rules on unhosted wallets and cross-border transfers—this seminar brings together regulators, law enforcement, financial institutions, and global tech leaders to bridge statutory requirements with operational industry practice. Event Highlights • Legislative Challenges & Risk Control • Legal issues in the full implementation of the Travel Rule and risk-based control practices for strengthening financial governance • Global Infrastructure & Tech Demonstration • Sumsub's compliance model supporting 2,000+ global clients and a remittance PoC case study integrating foreign national KYC • Public-Private Joint Panel Discussion • Strategies for operationalizing regulatory requirements into industry practice, featuring regulatory authorities, law enforcement, Korean financial institutions, and global experts

name: CyberSwaraj: Nostr, Cryptography Basics & How It Actually Works
description:
A beginner-to-intermediate friendly workshop for anyone curious about real digital privacy. Tired of platforms that own your data, shadow-ban your voice, or can disappear overnight? This hands-on session pulls back the curtain on Nostr — a simple, open protocol for decentralized social networking — and the cryptography that makes it possible. No prior technical background required; just curiosity

What You'll Learn Part 1 — Cryptography Basics (Demystified) • Why privacy isn't "having something to hide" — it's about control • Public vs. private keys: the foundation of digital identity • Hashing, signatures, and encryption — what they do and when to use each • How you already use this technology everyday without realizing it • Common myths about anonymity and what actually protects you Part 2 — What Is Nostr? • The problem Nostr solves: platform lock-in, censorship, and identity fragility • How Nostr works: events, relays, keys, and clients • Your keys = your identity. Your data = portable across apps • Practical setup: create your first identity and post your first note Part 3 — Nostr Technicals (Made Approachable) • Event structure and kinds — the grammar of the protocol • Relays: what they are, how to choose them, and why many is better than one • NIPs (Nostr Implementation Possibilities) — the standards that keep the network compatible • Zap (Lightning payments) basics and why they matter for creators • Security habits: key storage, signing devices, and avoiding common pitfall

Who This Is For • Beginners curious about privacy and decentralized tech • Builders, writers, and creators wanting platform independence • Intermediates who've "heard of Nostr" but never really understood it • Anyone who's lost an account, been shadow-banned, or worries about data ownershi

What You'll Walk Away With • A working Nostr identity and your first published note • A clear mental model of cryptography fundamentals • The confidence to evaluate privacy tools critically • Resources and a community to continue learnin

Format Interactive mini-lecture + live demos + guided setup time + Q&A. Bring a laptop or phone. No coding required to participate; code examples available for the curious. Privacy isn't a feature you buy — it's a skill you build. Come learn it with us

​Privacy is not about hiding. Most conversations about privacy start by making you feel paranoid. This one won't. Privacy is something ordinary and human. It's the ability to decide what parts of your life get shared, when they get shared, and with whom. In the physical world this feels obvious. You close the door when you change clothes. You lower your voice in a crowded room. You don't hand your diary to a stranger. Online, we've slowly given up all of that, usually without realising we were giving anything up. Each app asks for a small permission. Each service collects a small piece of information. Individually, none of it feels like much. Put together, it forms a surprisingly complete picture of how you live, think, move, and talk to people you love

​What is the 'CyberSwaraj' event series about CyberSwaraj is a gathering for anyone interested in digital privacy, open-source tools, and taking back some control over their digital life. We run sessions for beginners, workshops for people ready to go deeper, and occasional deep-dives for the technically curious. Developers, privacy advocates, and people who've simply had enough of being tracked are all welcome

Stay Connected • Join us on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@CyberSwara

name: L’écosystème fintech montréalais à l’heure de la tokenisation
description: La tokenisation n’est plus une promesse technologique. Les cadres réglementaires convergent aux États-Unis, en Europe, à Hong Kong et au Canada. Les institutions financières s’organisent en consortiums, et les stablecoins s’imposent progressivement comme de véritables rails de paiement. Montréal possède de solides atouts pour prendre part à cette transformation : un écosystème fintech mature, des talents spécialisés en finance et en technologies numériques, ainsi qu’une expertise reconnue en intelligence artificielle. La métropole bénéficie également d’un savoir-faire concret dans les domaines de la chaîne de blocs, du Web3 et de la DeFi, avec des entreprises et des équipes capables de mener des projets d’envergure au Québec comme à l’international. Lors de cet événement de la communauté CFI, Finance Montréal et T-RIZE présenteront les grandes tendances qui façonnent l’avenir de la finance numérique et discuteront du rôle que le Québec peut jouer dans le développement de l’économie tokenisée. À partir des faits saillants du Rapport Fintech Québec 2026 et d’une analyse des avancées récentes en matière de tokenisation, nous verrons pourquoi Montréal offre un environnement particulièrement favorable aux initiatives liées aux actifs numériques et aux infrastructures financières de nouvelle génération. Programme 1. Accueil et dîner 2. Présentation du Rapport Fintech Québec 2026 et portrait de l’écosystème fintech montréalais 3. L’écosystème montréalais de la tokenisation 4. Période de questions et échanges entre pairs Présentateurs • Bruno Séguin, directeur principal, Comptes stratégiques, Finance Montréal • Jean-Luc Pellerin, directeur, Écosystème et partenariats stratégiques, T-RIZE Ce que vous allez retirer de cet événement • Un portrait à jour de l’écosystème fintech montréalais, tiré du Rapport Fintech Québec 2026; • Un tour d’horizon des acteurs qui bâtissent l’infrastructure de tokenisation à Montréal. Un dîner sera servi sur place. L’événement est gratuit, mais les places sont limitées.

## CORGEAR Night vol.33 ～仮想NISHIと振り返る2026年のWeb3 — コーギアナイト忘年会～ 昨年の年末回で大好評だった「仮想NISHIと振り返るWeb3」を、今年も開催します！ 今回も暗号資産アナリストの仮想NISHI氏をお迎えし、2026年のWeb3・暗号資産市場を振り返ります。 暗号資産の制度整備や税制見直しに向けた動きが進み、ステーブルコインやRWAなど、既存金融との接点が広がった2026年。一方で、ビットコインをはじめとする暗号資産市場は大きく揺れ動き、期待と現実が交錯する一年となりました。 昨年に引き続き、チャートをもとに2026年の相場を振り返りながら、制度、技術、資金の流れ、そしてコミュニティの変化を読み解きます。 大幅な下落から夏場の反発まで、相場が大きく揺れた2026年。その一方で、ETFを通じた資金の流れや金融政策が市場を左右し、予測市場や資産のトークン化など、新たな動きも広がりました。相場の裏側では何が起きていたのか。仮想NISHI氏のチャート解説とともに一年を振り返り、2027年の暗号資産市場を展望します。 2026年を締めくくるこの夜は、年末恒例のコーギアナイト忘年会でもあります。 今年も少し早い乾杯とともに、クリプトの一年を振り返りましょう

name: CWC x Sosoul: A Breathwork Evening
description:
CWC x Sosoul: A Breathwork Evening Two hours, n

:
- , just space to breathe, slow down, and reset with the Crypto Women Collective community. About this event: When the week fills up, the first thing we drop is never the deadline. It's the twenty minutes we promised ourselves, the ones that don't belong to a client, a to-do list, or anyone but us. We thought this would be something for our members: a breathwork session hosted at the beautiful Sosoul Amsterdam (https://www.instagram.com/sosoul.nl/). No crypto talk, no networking pressure, just space to reset and be with other women from the community without a

:
- attached. Never done breathwork before? It's a guided practice using conscious breathing patterns to shift your nervous system out of fight-or-flight and into actual rest. No experience needed, you just show up and breathe

:
- Walk in between 19:30 and 20:00, doors close right at 20:00 when the breathwork starts. From there, our guide takes the group through a full breathwork practice designed to release tension you didn't even know you were holding, the kind that sitting still never quite reaches. Come as you are; loose, comfortable clothing helps. Mats and props are provided. Afterward, there's a few quiet minutes to notice how you feel, and time to talk with the person next to you or whoever's in the room, before we close out around 22:00. Your guide: Marieke Lintz (https://www.instagram.com/marieke.breathes/) is a breathwork coach and a CWC member herself. She'll lead the group through the practice and hold space for whatever comes up in the room. Details Thursday 10 December 19:30 doors · 20:00 breathwork starts · 22:00 end Sosoul, Anjeliersstraat 46-H, Amsterdam (https://www.instagram.com/sosoul.nl/) €27,50 for CWC members (usually €55) Max 12 spots Not yet part of the Crypto Women Collective? Crypto Women Collective is a growing community of 300+, from complete beginners to people already building careers in the space. This is a community of peers and women who want to know more, learn together and network, all around the topic of crypto and beyond. Become a member (https://tally.so/r/yPYd46) today. FAQ: Do I need any experience with breathwork? No. This session works whether you've never tried it or you do it every week. What should I bring or wear? Comfortable, loose-fitting clothing. Mats and props are provided at the venue. Can I arrive a little later than 19:30? Please don't leave it too late, doors close at 20:00 sharp when the breathwork begins, and once the practice starts we can't let latecomers in without disrupting the group. Good to know Photo & Video: We may take photos and video at this event for our website and social media. Prefer not to be photographed? Just let our team know on arrival. More on how we handle your data in our Privacy & Cookie Policy (https://cryptowomencollective.com/privacy-cookie-policy?utm_source=luma). Refunds: Plans change, we get it. You can cancel for a full refund until 2 December (7 days before the event). After that, we can't refund your ticket. We book and pay for the venue in advance, and with only 12 spots, every seat counts. Can't make it after all? You're welcome to pass your spot on to a friend, just let us know who's coming in your place. If we ever need to cancel, you'll get a full refund. As tickets are for a specific date, the 14-day withdrawal right doesn't apply. Staying in touch: With your ticket, you'll also receive occasional updates about upcoming CWC events. Not for you? Just unsubscribe in any email. By getting a ticket, you agree to our Terms & Conditions. Questions? Reach out at contact@cryptowomencollective.com, we're happy to help.

name: Bitcoin Book Club: Resistance Money
description:
Join the Bitcoin District Book Club! We meet every month to explore new rabbit holes by reading books that are popular with bitcoiners.

This December, we're reading Resistance Money: A Philosophical Case for Bitcoin by Andrew Bailey, Bradley Rettler, and Craig Warmke. We'll be joined by one of the authors, Andrew Bailey, for a live discussion.

The authors argue that bitcoin is "resistance money," a form of money that resists censorship, confiscation, and inflation. They make the case from philosophy, drawing on ideas about money, freedom, and justice.

Bring your questions for Andrew, whether you're a skeptic, a maximalist, or somewhere in between.

Get the book here: https://www.resistance.money/

Event Notes:

Discussion Starters: We'll open with a few key questions on the book's central arguments, then turn to Q&A with Andrew.

Future Reads: Have a book recommendation? Let us know and we'll add it to the list on our website.

Afterwards: Stick around to hang out, continue the conversation, and grab some food.

name: Workshop: Navigating Cyber Threats Across the Onchain Ecosystem
description:
Welcome to The Studio Workshop Series: sessions designed for founders who are building right now. Each workshop takes one skill that directly affects how you fundraise, grow, or ship, and breaks it down into concrete steps you can apply to your own startup. :
- : Doors open 5:30 PM: Workshop 6:30 PM: Networkin

About the workshop Every team building onchain is a target. Attackers move fast, from wallet drainers and fake tokens to exploits that trick users into signing something different from what they saw. The better you understand how these attacks work, the better you can design against them. Join Meg Yodfat and Noah Newfield from Blockaid (https://www.blockaid.io/) to break down the threats hitting builders today and how to stop them. We’ll walk through real attack patterns, map them to a security lifecycle for building dApps, from threat modeling and audits to deployment, and show how teams use real-time monitoring and transaction validation to protect protocols and users once they’re live. Bring your questions and a product or flow you’d like pressure-tested. We’ll use teams in the room as live case studies, and you’ll leave with a practical security checklist for your own build

About the speaker

Meg Yodfat (https://il.linkedin.com/in/megal-yodfat) Meg is Director of Customer Success at Blockaid, where she partners with every customer, from leading wallets and exchanges to chains and onchain protocols, to shape their security strategy and defend against threats ranging from wallet drainers and phishing to protocol exploits. She brings over a decade of experience in business development, partnerships, and revenue leadership. Before Blockaid, she was Head of Revenue at Infront Lab, led business development and partnerships at the blockchain startup Leeway, co-founded the startup Bobe

Noah Newfield (https://www.linkedin.com/in/noah-newfield-208a40129) Noah's been in crypto for 9+ years. He's worked on GTM at companies like Uniswap, Share, and Conduit. Prior to Blockaid he built a Stablecoin consumer company in YCombinator. He's now on the Customer Success team at Blockaid where he helps clients solve their most pressing security and business proble

About Blockaid Blockaid (https://www.blockaid.io/) is the security layer behind the world's leading crypto platforms, protecting users, assets, and business operations from fraud, exploits, and malicious activity at scale

About The Studio The Studio (https://thestudio.monad.xyz/?utm_source=luma)is Monad Foundation's founder workspace in the heart of Manhattan, where early-stage teams building on Monad work side by side. It is 100% equity-free: zero equity, zero fees. Teams get dedicated desks, hands-on support on pitch, GTM, and fundraising, and direct access to the VCs, angels, and mentors who work from the space alongside them. Interested in building on Monad and want in? Learn more and apply at https://thestudio.monad.xyz

​About Monad Foundation The Monad Foundation (https://www.monad.foundation/?utm_source=luma)is an independent organization dedicated to encouraging the development and adoption of the Monad blockchain protocol, an ultra-high-performant EVM L1 blockchain. Monad offers the best of both worlds: unrivaled performance (10,000 transactions per second) and portability (full-compatibility for Ethereum smart contracts)

name: Wealth Tech Executive Forum | 📍Dubai Edition
description:
🇦🇪 The Wealth Tech Executive Forum (https://wealthtech-executiveforum.com/?utm_source=luma): Dubai Edition is an exclusive, invite-only event tailored for senior executives who are driving the future of digital assets, institutional infrastructure, and capital allocation

ACTIONABLE INSIGHTS & LATEST TRENDS & HIGH-CLASS NETWORK As global financial markets undergo significant transformation, institutions are actively redefining their strategies concerning digital asset products, tokenization, custody solutions, market infrastructure, and institutional access. 🇦🇪 The UAE, a major financial center and one of the global leaders in digital asset innovation, offers the ideal environment for this critical dialogue. The event series is brought to you by CV VC (https://www.cvvc.com/?utm_source=luma), with SCRYPT (https://www.scrypt.swiss/?utm_source=luma) as the main partner, and in partnership with DMCC (https://dmcc.ae/ecosystems/wealth-hub)

Who is attending? This edition is designed to convene a select cohort of senior decision-makers, including executives from: • Banks and Private Banking • Asset Managers and Institutional Allocators • Family Office Principals (focused on digital assets) • Custody and Digital Asset Banking • Tokenization and Digital Securities Platforms • Institutional Trading and Market Infrastructure Providers • Hedge Fund Portfolio Manager

Core Themes for Discussion The focused content will explore the following key areas: • Allocator perspectives on digital asset exposure • Market structure, trading access, and execution • The pivotal role of wealth and private banking in the digital asset economy • Institutional digital asset infrastructure • Tokenization and digital securities • Custody and banking for digital asset

Event Format: Efficient and Focused The event format is intentionally compact and highly time-efficient. It is structured to combine focused keynote perspectives, panel discussions, audience Q&A, and exclusive, curated networking. This design allows participants to gain relevant insights and forge meaningful connections in a high-caliber setting without requiring a full day away from the office

Attendance Note Attendance is strictly limited and subject to approval to ensure a high-quality, peer-level exchange. Chatham rules apply

Other Editions in the Series: • Zurich (Concluded) (https://wealthtech-executiveforum.com/insights/zurich-edition) • Geneva (https://luma.com/4ppsu496) • Frankfurt (https://luma.com/icv7e9eu) • London (To be Confirmed) • Monaco (To Be Confirmed) Find out more on our website: https://wealthtech-executiveforum.com

What Comes Next? The Next Disruption in Asset Management? Asset management has evolved in distinct waves, each driven by structural innovation and enabled by technology: 1770s: Closed-End Funds 1920s: Open-End Mutual Funds 1970s: Index Funds 1990s: ETFs 2020s: A new paradigm emerging: Vaults? Technological innovations in digital trading and programmatic trading gave rise to ETFs in the 1990s, which now account for around $20 trillion in AUM. Technology continues to evolve, and with it comes the next major disruption in asset management. Is the next reinvention of asset management already unfolding before us? The real question is not whether asset management will continue to be reinvented, but which investors will identify the next structural change early enough to benefit from it? This forum will explore exactly that
